$comment:
The planet's winds, as a FEW DECLARED NUMBERS. tools/build-atlas.mjs grows the whole wind field from this file and the Atlas's own land, writes one wind per hex into data/maps/earth-atlas.json, and draws the streamlines from the same field. Nothing here names a hex or an ocean: change a number and every wind, lane and streamline moves together.

THE MODEL, in one paragraph. Along the surface the planet's air moves in belts that depend only on latitude (`profile`). That alone would blow straight through continents, so the belts are turned into a stream function - a height whose contours are the wind's paths - and that height is pulled down to nothing at every coast over `coastTaperKm`. A coast is then itself a path the wind follows, and the belts close up into loops round each ocean: clockwise in the north, anticlockwise in the south, round the high-pressure belt at about thirty degrees. That is the real shape of the trade winds and westerlies, and it is why a sailing ship bound from Europe to the Cape swings out towards Brazil.

profile.$comment: Eastward wind in m/s against latitude: negative blows from the east, positive from the west. Smooth between the points. Roughly the yearly average of the real surface wind over the oceans.

$coastTaperKmNote: How far out from a coast the wind is still bent along it. Shorter makes tight loops hugging every coast; longer lets the belts blow straight across a narrow sea.
$calmBelowMsNote: A hex whose wind is gentler than this is a CALM hex: the doldrums at the equator, the horse latitudes at thirty degrees.
$fullStrengthMsNote: A wind this strong or stronger has its whole effect on a sailing ship; a weaker one has a share of it.

belts.$comment: Names for the bands of latitude, used to label each hex's wind and to put the names on the board. `side` says which hemisphere a label is for; a belt with `calm` is labelled where the wind dies, not on a streamline.

exampleRule.$comment: AN EXAMPLE, NOT A RULE YET. What a step of one Atlas hex costs a sailing ship, in rounds, by the wind in the hex it leaves. It is here so the lanes can be sailed and the digital game can try it; no rules chapter prints it until it is adopted.
exampleRule.how: Take the angle between the way the ship steps and the way the wind blows. Straight downwind costs withWind, square across costs across, dead into it costs againstWind, smoothly between; a wind weaker than fullStrengthMs moves the cost only that share of the way from across. A calm hex costs calm whichever way the ship goes.

streamlines.$comment: How the picture is drawn, and nothing else: the field is the same whichever numbers are here.
